steps: Open a terminal, go to any folder, and type "agi" then press Enter.
Look at the first screen: it shows "Welcome to AGI", the Model and Folder rows, and no earlier messages.
Check that the composer is ready for typing below the start content.
Type "/new" and press Enter, then confirm the conversation area is empty again.
S12.01.where: Run "agi" in a folder; the first screen shows "Welcome to AGI" with an empty chat area and the composer. Type "/new" ("Start a new conversation") to get a fresh empty chat.

labels.text: Show or set how replies address you and read (/personalize set <field> <value>)

S12.03.note: No greeting line with a name was found in the start-screen code, so the neutral-greeting check may only be a no-name check. The /personalize description is the only personal-setting text found.
steps: Type "agi" in a terminal and look at the first screen: the code shows "Welcome to AGI", Model and Folder rows and no name line.
Type "/personalize" to see how replies address you and check that no personal detail appears on the new-chat screen.
Compare with Expected: the greeting should be neutral with no personal details.
S12.03.where: Run "agi" (start screen shows "Welcome to AGI"); personal-name setting is under "/personalize".

labels.text: List the folders you worked in most recently, to start a session in one with agi -C.

S12.06.needs: a folder you have worked in before
S12.06.note: The code gives a command-line list only. The start screen's "Recent activity" shows sessions, not projects. Searched apps/cli/src for recent-project shortcuts on the start screen; none found.
steps: Type "agi projects recent" in a terminal and press Enter.
Read the list of folders it prints (default limit 10).
Compare with Expected: the code only lists folders for "agi -C"; it does not open a project or start a chat from the new-chat screen.
S12.06.where: "agi projects recent" in a terminal lists recent folders; no recent-project shortcut was found on the new-chat screen.

S12.07.needs: a folder with recently edited files
S12.07.note: Ordering is by file modification time (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs), not recently used files. The picker label text was not found as a literal string.
steps: Start "agi" in a git folder where you changed a few files recently.
Type "@" in the composer.
Look at the picker: the most recently modified files should appear at the top.
Compare with Expected: the code ranks by file modification time, not by files you used in chat, so a file you only read will not move up.
S12.07.where: In the composer, type "@" to open the file picker; recently changed files are listed first.

labels.text: Usage: /search <question>, answer from a web search

steps: Start "agi" and type "/search" followed by a question, for example "/search latest release notes".
Press Enter to send.
Look for the answer to be based on a web search (the code sets a flag so only the next message searches).
Compare with Expected: the search should apply to that one message only.
S12.10.where: Type "/search <question>" in the composer and press Enter.

labels.text: Nothing generated yet. Try /image a red bicycle.

S12.12.note: No separate image mode was found; the entry is the /image command.
steps: Start "agi" and type "/image a red bicycle" then press Enter.
Wait for the generated image to appear, shown as an image chip.
Type "/image open" to open the last generated image.
Compare with Expected: the code has no image-creation mode; it is a one-shot command, so check whether the send generates an image as described.
S12.12.where: Type "/image <prompt>" in the composer and press Enter (alias "/imagine").

S12.14.note: The code has both a dictate path and run_voice_mode; the help text describes voice input only.
steps: Start "agi" and type "/voice" then press Enter.
Speak into the microphone when prompted.
Check that your speech is turned into text and a spoken conversation can run.
Compare with Expected: the code's help text says "Toggle voice input", so confirm it starts a voice conversation rather than only input.
S12.14.where: Type "/voice" in the composer (alias "/v") to start voice input or voice mode.

labels.text: Plan a goal into steps and run them as subagents

S12.15.note: Agentic work is reached through slash commands, not a mode choice on the new-chat screen. Whether a blocker applies in a given session was not checked.
steps: Start "agi" and type "/workflow" to see the usage text.
Type "/workflow <a goal>" and press Enter.
Check that the goal is broken into steps and run as subagents.
Compare with Expected: the code may refuse the workflow with a blocker message (workflow_blocker), which should be shown on screen.
S12.15.where: Type "/workflow <goal>" in the composer; "/bg <instruction>" and "/thread <instruction>" are related entries.

steps: Open a terminal, go to a code project folder, and type "agi".
Look at the first screen for the "Folder" row showing this project path.
Type a coding request, for example "list the files in this project".
Compare with Expected: the agent should work on this repository.
S12.16.where: Run "agi" inside a project folder (or "agi -C <folder>"); the start screen shows the Folder row.

S12.17.note: Searched apps/cli/src for "temporary", "incognito" and "private": no in-chat control found. The flag help is "Disable session persistence for this run." (apps/cli/src/cli_options.rs).
steps: Type "agi --no-session-persistence" in a terminal and start a chat.
Check whether the chat is kept in history afterwards (for example with "/history").
Compare with Expected: the code only offers this as a launch flag for the whole run, not a switch before or during a chat.
S12.17.where: Launch with "agi --no-session-persistence" (flag only); no in-chat temporary switch was found.

steps: Type "agi" and look at the first screen's Model row.
Read the model name shown next to it.
Type "/model" to see the model list and compare the name with what the next message will use.
Compare with Expected: the model name should be visible before you send a message.
S12.18.where: Run "agi"; the first screen shows the Model row with the model name, and the status line shows it too.

labels.text: Link this directory to an account project by id or name.

S12.20.note: No project picker on the new-chat screen was found; searched apps/cli/src for project selection before sending.
steps: In a terminal, go to the folder for the new chat.
Type "agi projects link <project id or name>" and press Enter.
Type "agi" and check the first screen for the Folder row and the linked project.
Compare with Expected: the project should be chosen before sending; the code links a folder, not a chat, from the command line.
S12.20.where: Type "agi projects link <project>" in the folder you want to use (no in-chat project picker was found).

labels.text: read-only tools only, no file edits. The model plans before acting.

S12.21.note: Mode explanations come from mode_description; no examples were found in the code. The banner appears after cycling, not necessarily on the first screen.
steps: Start "agi" and press Shift+Tab once.
Read the banner that appears, which names the mode and explains it.
Press Shift+Tab again to cycle through the other modes.
Compare with Expected: each explanation should appear, but the code has no example text for each mode.
S12.21.where: Press Shift+Tab on the chat screen to cycle modes; a banner shows each mode's explanation.

S12.22.needs: a fresh install (first-run setup not yet done)
S12.22.note: Searched apps/cli/src/onboarding.rs for "tour", "tips" and feature text: none found. The banner text (print_welcome_banner) was not read in full.
steps: Remove the setup marker or use a fresh install, then type "agi".
Read the welcome banner and each setup step.
Compare with Expected: the code shows setup choices only; no short feature introduction was found.
S12.22.where: First-run setup when "agi" is started for the first time (steps: welcome banner, trust this folder, choose auth, model, effort, permission mode).

labels.text: Sign in to get started, open to everyone

S12.24.needs: a fresh install and no account
S12.24.note: No guest usage limit text was found in the code searched; the only sign-in text is the auth choice and "not signed in (agi login)" in the status line (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs).
steps: Start "agi" for the first time and continue to the auth choice.
Choose "Skip for now" and start a chat.
Check whether a sign-in prompt or limit message appears, and compare with Expected.
Type "/login" to see the sign-in route.
S12.24.where: First-run setup, choose "Skip for now" or "AGI cloud" (Sign in to get started, open to everyone).
